text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The permanent five members of the Security Council call on the two sides to start direct talks in June.
- Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos receives a warm welcome in Turkey.
- U.N. big five call on the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides to prepare for talks.
- Weeping icon in a refugee estate outside Nicosia is a sign of "good news", says its priest.
- The permanent five turn their attention to achieving progress in the United Nations proximity talks in preparation of a summit between the two sides.
- The United Nations are preparing for a summit between the leaders of the two sides in June.
- The government-run programming bureau forecasts 3.5 percent GDP growth in 1997, with unemployment at 3.2 percent and inflation at 3 percent.

- A Russian document outlining the basic principles for a solution to the Cyprus dispute will be used by the government to balance ideas of former U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, perceived as containing negative elements by the Greek Cypriot side.
- The American government is trying to cover up the results of an official inquiry into the fate of five Americans of Cypriot origin who disappeared during the Turkish invasion in 1974.
